content.value_statement: Project teams often lose consistency across branches, documentation, configuration, and reviews. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code shared guidance for development conventions.
actual_capabilities: Guides project file and directory organization.
Supports commit messages, pull requests, and branch workflow consistency.
Helps maintain README, contribution, changelog, and release documentation.
Advises on environment variables, settings files, secrets management, and feature flags.
Supports dependency file updates and testing requirements before merges.
limitations: Provides conventions only; it does not include executable automation or validation scripts.
Depends on a referenced conventions document outside the skill file.
Does not define language-specific coding standards beyond project organization topics.
Does not replace team approval for secret handling or release decisions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Repository
use_cases.description: Set up directory structure, README content, dependency files, and review expectations before the first merge.

use_cases.title: Keep Team Workflow Consistent
use_cases.description: Apply shared rules for branches, commit messages, pull requests, tests, and changelog updates.

use_cases.title: Document Configuration Practices
use_cases.description: Create guidance for environment variables, feature flags, and settings files without exposing secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Project Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository structure and suggest changes that match the global-conventions skill. Focus on directories, README coverage, and dependency files.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Git Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write branch, commit, pull request, testing, and changelog conventions for this project.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Configuration Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a convention plan for environment variables, settings files, feature flags, and secrets handling. Include review checkpoints and documentation owners.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether this project follows global conventions before release. Review documentation, dependencies, tests, branching rules, and release notes. List gaps by priority.

output_examples.input: Review our repository organization before onboarding new developers.
output: Recommended a clearer folder layout for source, tests, documentation, and configuration.
Identified missing README sections for setup, contribution steps, and dependency updates.

output_examples.input: Create pull request conventions for a small service team.
output: A concise workflow covering branch names, commit messages, review expectations, test evidence, and changelog updates.
A checklist that reviewers can apply before merge approval.

output_examples.input: Document configuration and secret handling rules.
output: Guidance separates public settings from sensitive values.
Secret names, ownership, and rotation expectations are documented without exposing actual secret values.

best_practices: Keep conventions near the workflows they govern and review them with code changes.
Treat secrets as sensitive values; document names and purpose without copying values.
Update README, changelog, and dependency notes in the same change when behavior shifts.
anti_patterns: Linking to unreviewed parent-directory files instead of packaging required guidance.
Mixing team workflow policy with private secret values or local-only settings.
Letting branch, commit, and review rules drift across repositories.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps teams apply consistent conventions for repository structure, Git workflow, documentation, configuration, dependencies, and reviews.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The visible skill provides written guidance, not scripts or automation.

faq.question: Can it manage secrets?
faq.answer: It can help document safe handling practices, but it should not reveal or copy secret values.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include all referenced guidance?
faq.answer: No. It points to a parent-directory conventions file, so package completeness should be checked.

faq.question: Is it language-specific?
faq.answer: No. It covers repository and team workflow conventions rather than a specific programming language.
